Lessons.Title: Grams and Kilograms, Liters and Milliliters
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will describe the relationship between liters and milliliters and between kilograms and grams, and to express each of the larger units in terms of the smaller units.
Core relationship: Grams/kilograms and liters/milliliters. Use 1 kg = 1,000 g and 1 L = 1,000 mL; context decides weight or capacity.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Which One Doesn’t Belong: Meter, Meter on the Page	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  A Whole Lot of Paper Clips	 (15 minutes); Activity 2:  Liters and Milliliters	 (20 minutes); Cool-down:  A Chef and a Host	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: How many grams are in 2 kilograms?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): How many milliliters are in 3 liters?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
